args.title: checkout-api unhealthy on v2.3.1 — rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. Error rate peaked at 18% and the service reported healthy=false.

Action taken: Rolled production back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy status in production (v2.2.9 and v2.3.0 both healthy; v2.3.1 marked unhealthy). Note: the first rollback attempt failed with a partial_failure ("Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error"), leaving the fleet in a mixed state (us-east=v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west=v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout successfully.

Current state: All three production regions are on v2.3.0, service healthy=true, error rate 0.002.

Since v2.3.1 has been observed unhealthy in production it should not be redeployed without change-manager approval and a root-cause investigation. Follow-up needed: determine why v2.3.1 fails health checks, and investigate the orchestrator error that interrupted the first rollback attempt.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did go through — INC-0001 exists, so no retry was needed.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with `healthy=false` and an 18% error rate. Deployment history showed v2.3.1 as unhealthy, with v2.3.0 and v2.2.9 both healthy — making **v2.3.0** the most recent production-healthy release.

**Rollback:** The first attempt returned a `partial_failure` ("Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error"), which left the fleet split — us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west were still running the bad v2.3.1. I checked state before retrying, then re-ran the rollback to v2.3.0, which completed across all regions.

**Verified state:** All three regions on v2.3.0, `healthy=true`, error rate down to 0.002 (from 0.18).

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) documenting the timeline, including the partial-failure detail and current recovery state. The `create_incident` call timed out on the response, but I confirmed via `list_incidents` that the incident was recorded — I did not re-submit, which avoided a duplicate page to on-call.

**Two follow-ups worth flagging:**
- The orchestrator error that halted the first rollback is unexplained and could cause future rollouts to stall mid-fleet — worth investigating on its own.
- I did not attempt to redeploy v2.3.1; per policy it now requires change-manager approval since it has never been healthy in production.
